name: Softminal Cache
author: Softminal

sections.description:
Features | Blog | Get Support

Softminal Cache makes your site fast and keeps it safe while doing so. 🛡️ Risky changes are checked on your own site right after you save them, and every change can be undone.

🎁 100% free, forever. There is no Pro version, no upsell, no ads and no account. Every feature is in this plugin, and nothing leaves your server.

🧩 More from Softminal

  • ImageCraft – image optimizer: compression, WebP & AVIF, AI alt text and titles, SEO file names and an image SEO audit. Works side by side with Softminal Cache.
  • B2B Suite for WooCommerce – wholesale prices, customer-group pricing, trade registration, quantity rules and a bulk order form.

⚡ Page cache

  • Pages are stored the first time they are built and served to the next visitors before WordPress loads, through a standard advanced-cache.php drop-in. If the drop-in cannot be installed, pages are still served from inside WordPress.
  • Clears itself when you publish or update content, approve a comment, change the theme, menus or widgets, or install updates. Purge everything or one page from the plugin screen or the admin bar.
  • Separate copy for phones, serve the old copy while rebuilding (stale-while-revalidate), and optional caching of 404 pages, feeds and logged-in users (private per-session copies, never for editors or administrators).
  • Keep pages from 1 hour to 7 days; exclude URLs with wildcards or regular expressions; add your own never-cache cookies; tracking parameters such as utm_*, fbclid and gclid share one cached copy.
  • Cache rules: keep some pages for a different time (from 15 minutes to 7 days, by address pattern), never cache for chosen browsers or apps (user agent), clear extra pages whenever a post is updated, and tick Don’t cache this page on any single post or page.
  • Widget and fragment cache: reuse the output of classic widgets, and of any slow part of a page with the softminal_cache_fragment() helper, even on pages that can’t be cached as a whole (logged-in users, carts). Emptied with the page cache.
  • Multilingual sites (WPML, Polylang): a homepage that redirects by browser language is never cached, translations are cleared together, and preload covers every language.
  • Preload rebuilds pages in the background from your sitemap (or your homepage links), at a speed set from your host’s limits.
  • Browser cache and compression rules for Apache and LiteSpeed, and a snippet to copy for Nginx.
  • Redis object cache: one switch after a connection test (address or socket, database, password stored encrypted, key prefix, TLS). Never replaces another object cache, only clears this site’s keys, and pages keep working if Redis goes down.

✨ Optimize

  • JavaScript: minify, load scripts after the page is visible (defer, WordPress 6.3+), wait for the visitor before running scripts (delay, cookie banners kept working), remove jQuery Migrate, combine neighbouring files, with an exclusion list.
  • Speed hints: connect early to other sites (preconnect, DNS prefetch, suggested from the speed audit), load chosen files first (preload), and open the next page before the click (WordPress 6.8+ speculative loading, configured; a tiny hover-prefetch script on older versions).
  • CSS: minify stylesheets and inline styles, combine neighbouring files, with an exclusion list. Critical CSS and remove unused CSS, generated in your own browser from sample pages of your site (no cloud service): the first screen’s styles go into the page, and each stylesheet can be replaced by just the rules your pages use, with the full file loading on the visitor’s first scroll or tap.
  • Cloudflare and Varnish: clear them whenever this cache is cleared (API token stored encrypted).
  • CDN: serve images, styles, scripts, fonts and media from one or more pull-zone CDN addresses, with a Test button and an exclusion list.
  • HTML: minify the page itself (spaces and comments), leaving code blocks, text boxes, scripts and styles as they are.
  • Fonts: host Google Fonts on your own site, show text while fonts load (font-display: swap), preload the main fonts.
  • Images: lazy-load images, videos and embeds (the first pictures always load at once), add missing width and height, WebP and AVIF copies of new uploads served through <picture> (when your server supports them; the screen shows it), convert existing images in the background, a media audit for huge images and missing alt text, a YouTube preview that loads the player only on click, lazy background images, the main image loaded first (preload), and lazy render for far-down sections.
  • Compress and resize new and existing JPEG and PNG uploads on your own server (GD or Imagick, no cloud), with the original kept so you can restore it, and a Resize button for huge images in the media audit. Gravatar pictures can be kept on your own site.
  • Script Manager: turn any script or stylesheet off everywhere, only on certain pages, or for logged-in users only. Files other files need are never removed.
  • Bloat: remove the emoji script, embeds, Dashicons for visitors, XML-RPC, head clutter, self-pingbacks and version numbers; slow down Heartbeat; limit revisions; turn off RSS feeds, Google Fonts added through WordPress and block styles on pages without blocks; close the WordPress REST API to logged-out visitors; load WooCommerce’s cart fragments, styles and scripts only on shop pages; set the editor’s autosave interval.

🧹 Database

  • Clean post revisions (keeping the newest ones; autosaves are always kept), auto-drafts, trashed posts and comments, spam, expired transients, pingbacks, and data left behind by deleted posts, comments, users and categories, with a confirmation step and a scheduled clean-up (daily, weekly or monthly).
  • Optimise tables and convert old MyISAM tables to InnoDB, each with a dry run first.
  • See where your database space goes, which options are loaded on every page, and which scheduled tasks are stuck.

📊 Dashboard, profiles and safety

  • Speed audit with a score out of 100, measured on your own site in your browser: page load, server response, page weight, requests and the largest image, each with its change since the first audit, a Fix button on each finding and Fix all safe ones in one click.
  • Quick actions on the Dashboard: purge the cache, start a preload, test the cache, and jump to the settings you use most.
  • Profiles: Safe (the default), Balanced and Aggressive, with a table of what each one turns on.
  • Self-check: after a change that could break pages, the plugin loads your homepage and a post, watches for errors, and switches the change back by itself if the site got worse.
  • Undo the latest change for 24 hours, a full settings history to restore any earlier one, and Safe Mode to pause every optimisation while you check something (the page cache keeps working).
  • Detects other caching plugins and host caches (Kinsta, WP Engine, Flywheel, Pressable) and stays out of their way; detects other optimisation plugins and leaves their area to them.

🧰 Tools

  • Import settings from WP Rocket, and (beta) from LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Autoptimize and Perfmatters. You see what came over and can undo it.
  • Factory reset (undoable), and a Purge menu in the admin bar for the roles you choose (editors, shop managers…).
  • Export and import settings as a JSON file; a debug log of what the cache did; a config file (wp-content/softminal-cache.json) for sites managed from code; WP-CLI commands (wp softminal-cache purge|preload|status|db clean|settings export|import).

🤖 AI access (off by default)

  • Connect an AI app such as Claude or ChatGPT and ask about your cache in plain words: “Is my homepage cached?”, “What should I fix first?”, “Clear the shop page”.
  • Paste one address into the app and click Allow in your own WordPress. Developer tools (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code) connect with a token instead.
  • You choose what each app may do: only look, or look and make changes. Every change goes into the settings history and can be undone.
  • Risky actions (database cleanup, restoring old settings, imports, the object cache, CDN and Script Manager settings) wait for your approval in WordPress before they run.
  • Every action an AI app takes is listed under AI → Activity. API keys and passwords are never shown to an AI app, and you can disconnect any app in one click.
  • Built on the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), on your own site, with no account or service of ours in between.

🌍 Languages

The plugin screen is translated into Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Dutch. Help translate it into your language on translate.wordpress.org.

🔒 Never cached, automatically

So carts, logins and private pages always stay correct:

  • Logged-in users (unless you turn on their private copies) and recent commenters.
  • Cart, checkout, account and receipt pages of WooCommerce, FluentCart and Easy Digital Downloads, and shoppers who have a cart.
  • Search results, previews, password-protected and private pages, page-builder editors.
  • Form submissions and any request that isn’t a normal page view; pages that set a cookie.
  • Any page where another plugin asks for no caching with the standard DONOTCACHEPAGE constant.

🤝 Contribute

Softminal Cache is developed and maintained by Softminal. Contributions are welcome: report a bug, suggest a feature or send a pull request on GitHub.

If another caching plugin is active, deactivate it first; two page caches fight each other.

Third-party services

Softminal Cache collects no data and has no service of its own. Only the features below make outside requests, and only after you turn them on:

  • Test cache, Preload, speed audit, self-check: these load pages of your own site (home_url()). Nothing goes anywhere else.
  • CDN (Cache → CDN, off by default): the Test button loads one WordPress core file (wp-includes/js/jquery/jquery.min.js) from the CDN address you entered. When the CDN is on, visitors load your files from that CDN, under its own terms and privacy policy. The plugin sends it nothing else.
  • Cloudflare (Cache → CDN, Cloudflare and Bunny, off until you connect): with your API token, the plugin calls api.cloudflare.com. It finds your site’s zone and clears Cloudflare’s cache when this plugin clears its own (changed page addresses, or everything). Nothing else is sent. Cloudflare terms and privacy policy.
  • Bunny (Cache → CDN, Cloudflare and Bunny, off until you connect): with your API key, the plugin calls api.bunny.net. It finds the pull zone for this site and clears it when this plugin clears everything. Nothing else is sent. If you use that pull zone as your CDN, visitors load your files from Bunny. bunny.net terms and privacy policy.
  • Keep Gravatar pictures on your site (Optimize → Images, off by default): your server downloads each Gravatar picture once from secure.gravatar.com, the address WordPress already uses. It then serves the picture from your site and refreshes it weekly. Nothing else is sent. Gravatar terms and privacy policy.
  • Google PageSpeed (Dashboard, only when you click Check with Google): the plugin sends one of your page addresses and your free Google API key to www.googleapis.com. Google tests that page and sends back the results, which stay on your site. Nothing runs in the background. PageSpeed Insights API terms and Google’s privacy policy.
  • Host Google Fonts on your site (Optimize → Fonts, off by default): your server downloads the fonts your theme already uses from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, once. Your site then serves them, so visitors stop connecting to Google. Google Fonts terms and privacy policy.

  • AI access (the AI tab, off by default): the plugin never calls an AI service itself. When you connect an AI app (for example Claude by Anthropic, ChatGPT by OpenAI, or Cursor or VS Code with the model you choose), that app sends requests to your site. The plugin answers only what the app is allowed to see:

    • cache status and settings (never API keys, tokens or passwords)
    • page check, speed audit and PageSpeed results
    • settings history and database counts
    • the last lines of the debug log, if it is on, with secrets removed

    This information goes to the company behind the app, under its own terms and privacy policy: Anthropic terms and privacy policy, OpenAI terms and privacy policy. Apps that connect by address sign in with standard OAuth 2.1. You approve them on a page of your own WordPress, and their key works only for this site and only for what you allowed. Disconnect any app under AI → Connected apps.
sections.faq:
Does it work with WooCommerce and FluentCart?

Yes. Cart, checkout, account and receipt pages are never cached, and visitors who have a cart always get a live page, so nobody ever sees someone else’s cart.

Why does it change wp-config.php?

WordPress only loads a page cache early (before plugins and themes) when WP_CACHE is on. Softminal Cache adds define( 'WP_CACHE', true ); // Added by Softminal Cache near the top, and removes exactly that line when you deactivate it. If the file can’t be written, nothing breaks: pages are still cached from inside WordPress, and the plugin screen shows the line so you can add it yourself.

Where are cached pages stored?

In wp-content/cache/softminal-cache/ (each site has its own folder on a network). To use another folder, add define( 'SOFTMINAL_CACHE_CACHE_DIR', '/full/path/' ); to wp-config.php. Minified files, font copies and WebP/AVIF images are kept in wp-content/cache/softminal-cache-assets/ and next to the original images.

How do I check that a page came from the cache?

Open the page in a private window and look at the response headers: X-Softminal-Cache: HIT means it came from the cache, MISS means it was built and stored, and BYPASS: reason says why it wasn’t cached. The Dashboard’s Test cache does this for you.

Does it work on Nginx, Apache and LiteSpeed?

Yes. Pages are served by PHP, so no server rules are needed for caching. Browser-cache and compression rules are written to .htaccess on Apache and LiteSpeed; on Nginx the plugin gives you a snippet to add to your server block. On Nginx, also add the snippet’s deny rules: Apache reads the cache folder’s .htaccess, Nginx does not, and the rules keep the cache folder and the config file from being opened directly.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site keeps its own settings and cached pages, and pages are served from inside WordPress. Table changes (optimise, InnoDB conversion) need a network administrator.

Does it work with other image plugins?

Yes. If ImageCraft, ShortPixel, Performance Lab or Modern Image Formats already makes WebP/AVIF copies, Softminal Cache leaves image formats to that plugin and its Dashboard says “Handled by” that plugin. Compression steps aside the same way for Smush, ShortPixel, Imagify, EWWW, TinyPNG, reSmush.it, Optimole and ImageCraft. Lazy loading and image sizes still work.

I use a host with its own page cache.

Managed hosts such as Kinsta, WP Engine, Flywheel and Pressable already cache pages; Softminal Cache detects them, keeps its page cache off and still runs every other optimisation.

Will it break my site?

Every risky change is checked on your site right after you save it and switched back by itself if your homepage or a post got worse. If something still looks wrong, click Undo, turn on Safe Mode, or Purge.

Does the plugin send anything anywhere?

No. There is no account, no telemetry and no external service. See “Third-party services” below for the optional ones you turn on (Google Fonts download, your CDN, Cloudflare, Bunny, Google PageSpeed, and the AI apps you connect).

How do I connect Claude or ChatGPT?

Open Softminal Cache → AI and switch on Let AI apps use Softminal Cache. Copy the address shown there. In Claude, open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, paste the address and click Connect; in ChatGPT, add it as a custom connector (where this is depends on your ChatGPT plan; it may need developer mode). A page from your own WordPress opens: choose Only look or Look and make changes, then click Allow. Your site must be online on https for this. For Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code, open For developers on the same screen, create a token and copy the ready-made setup. To disconnect an app, click Revoke under AI → Connected apps.

Can an AI app break my site?

Only if you allow changes, and even then each change can be undone. Risky actions wait for your approval, the self-check switches a change back if your homepage or a post gets worse, and AI apps can never see or change API keys, passwords, the AI settings themselves, or files on your server.

How do I remove it completely?

Deactivate it to remove the drop-in, the WP_CACHE line, the .htaccess rules and all cached pages. Delete it to also remove its settings, its history table, its cache folders and the WebP/AVIF copies it made (copies made by another image plugin are left alone). To keep the settings when deleting, add define( 'SOFTMINAL_CACHE_KEEP_DATA_ON_UNINSTALL', true ); to wp-config.php. If you compressed images, the untouched originals of images you still have stay in wp-content/uploads/softminal-cache-originals/ so they are never lost (originals of deleted images are removed); delete that folder yourself when you no longer need them. Apache and LiteSpeed never serve that folder; on Nginx, add location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/softminal-cache-originals/ { deny all; }.

  • New: never cache for chosen browsers or apps.

  • New: a Resize button for huge images in the media audit.
  • New: keep Gravatar pictures on your own site.
  • New: clean data left behind by deleted comments, users and categories.
  • New: more bloat options, including RSS feeds, Google Fonts and WooCommerce cart fragments.
  • New: factory reset, with Undo.
  • New: a Purge menu in the admin bar for the roles you choose.
  • New: support for WPML and Polylang sites.
  • New: translated into Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Dutch.
  • Improved: a simpler Dashboard with quick actions and “Fix all safe ones”.
  • Fixed: speed changes are green only when the site got faster.

1.1.2 – 29 Oct, 2026

  • New: Critical CSS, generated in your own browser from sample pages of your site (no cloud service). The first screen’s styles go into the page and the full stylesheets load without holding it back.
  • New: Remove unused CSS, generated the same way. Each stylesheet is replaced by just the rules your pages use; the full file loads on the visitor’s first scroll or tap. Pages that no longer match keep their normal CSS until you generate again.
  • New: Redis object cache with a connection test, encrypted password, key prefix, database, socket and TLS. It never replaces another object cache, only clears this site’s keys, and pages keep working if Redis goes down.
  • New: Speed hints: connect early to other sites (preconnect and DNS prefetch, suggested by the speed audit) and load chosen files first (preload).
  • New: Open the next page before the click (speculative loading), using WordPress’s own on 6.8+ and a tiny script on older versions.
  • New: YouTube preview: the video’s picture and a play button; the player loads only when someone clicks.
  • New: Lazy background images: backgrounds set on a section load as it comes into view.
  • New: Main image loaded first (preload LCP image).
  • New: Lazy render: far-down sections are drawn only when the visitor gets near them.
  • Improved: the Cache tab is split into sections (Page cache, Browser and server, CDN and Cloudflare, Object cache).
  • Improved: calmer focus style on text fields, and a plug icon on the Cloudflare Connect button.
  • Profiles: Balanced now adds critical CSS, the YouTube preview and the main image preload; Aggressive adds all the new options. If you use one of these profiles, choose it again after updating to get them.

1.1.1 – 27 Oct, 2026

  • Security (multisite only): only a network admin can change the CDN address, because every script of the site loads from it. Site admins can still choose the file types and exclusions.
  • Security (multisite only): a Cloudflare token set in wp-config.php is shared by the whole network, so only a network admin can connect, disconnect, switch purging or clear the whole zone with it. A purge started by a site admin clears only that site’s pages.
  • Single sites are not affected.

1.1.0 – 27 Oct, 2026

  • New: CDN. Serve images, styles, scripts, fonts and media from up to five pull-zone CDN addresses, with a Test button, file types and an exclusion list (Cache tab).
  • New: Cloudflare and Varnish. Clear them whenever this plugin clears its cache: changed pages by address, or everything. The Cloudflare API token is stored encrypted, or set in wp-config.php (Cache tab).
  • New: delay JavaScript until the visitor scrolls, taps or presses a key. jQuery, cookie banners and your exclusions keep running at once; logged-in users are not affected (Optimize → JavaScript → Advanced).
  • New: combine CSS and combine JS. Neighbouring files become one without changing their order (Optimize → CSS / JavaScript → Advanced).
  • New: minify HTML. Spaces and comments are removed; code blocks, text boxes, scripts and styles are left as they are (Optimize → CSS → HTML).
  • The Aggressive profile now includes delay JS and combine CSS/JS. A site that used Aggressive shows “Custom” until it picks Aggressive again.
  • Importers carry over these settings from WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Autoptimize and Perfmatters.
  • Fix: relative image and font addresses inside a stylesheet linked as /wp-content/… now keep working after minify.
  • A small card on the plugin screen asks for a review a week after you start using the plugin. “Maybe later” asks again in two weeks; “Write a review” or “I already did” ends it.
  • Help: the “More from Softminal” text now says each plugin has a free version on WordPress.org.

1.0.0 – 25 Oct, 2026

  • Optimize: minify and defer JavaScript, remove jQuery Migrate, minify CSS, local Google Fonts with swap and preload, lazy loading and missing image sizes, WebP/AVIF copies of uploads with bulk conversion and a media audit, Script Manager, Bloat removal.
  • Cache: separate copy for phones, stale-while-revalidate, 404 and feed caching, logged-in private copies, regular-expression exclusions, custom never-cache cookies and ignored parameters, preload from the sitemap, browser-cache and compression rules.
  • Database: clean-up with confirmation and schedule, table optimise and InnoDB conversion with dry runs, autoloaded options, stuck scheduled tasks.
  • Dashboard: speed audit with score, history and Fix buttons; Safe, Balanced and Aggressive profiles; self-check that undoes a change that broke the site; Undo for 24 hours and a settings history with Restore; Safe Mode.
  • Help: a ? button in the top bar opens the docs, blog, support and more free plugins from Softminal.
  • Tools: importers for seven other plugins (six of them in beta), settings history with pages, settings export/import, debug log, config file, WP-CLI.
  • Security: pages that set a cookie are never stored, full-length atomic writes, per-site cache and file folders on a network, private logged-in copies tied to WordPress’s secret keys, wp-config.php edits written owner-only.

0.1.0 – 19 Oct, 2026

  • First release: page cache served before WordPress loads, Test cache, automatic clearing, Purge from the plugin screen and admin bar, cache lifetime and URL exclusions, safe handling of carts, logins and private pages, light and dark mode.

  • Self-check: after a change that could break pages, the plugin loads your homepage and a post, watches for errors, and switches the change back by itself if the site got worse.
  • Undo the latest change for 24 hours, a full settings history to restore any earlier one, and Safe Mode to pause every optimisation while you check something (the page cache keeps working).
  • Detects other caching plugins and host caches (Kinsta, WP Engine, Flywheel, Pressable) and stays out of their way; detects other optimisation plugins and leaves their area to them.

🧰 Tools

  • Import settings from WP Rocket, and (beta) from LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Autoptimize and Perfmatters. You see what came over and can undo it.
  • Factory reset (undoable), and a Purge menu in the admin bar for the roles you choose (editors, shop managers…).
  • Export and import settings as a JSON file; a debug log of what the cache did; a config file (wp-content/softminal-cache.json) for sites managed from code; WP-CLI commands (wp softminal-cache purge|preload|status|db clean|settings export|import).

🤖 AI access (off by default)

  • Connect an AI app such as Claude or ChatGPT and ask about your cache in plain words: “Is my homepage cached?”, “What should I fix first?”, “Clear the shop page”.
  • Paste one address into the app and click Allow in your own WordPress. Developer tools (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code) connect with a token instead.
  • You choose what each app may do: only look, or look and make changes. Every change goes into the settings history and can be undone.
  • Risky actions (database cleanup, restoring old settings, imports, the object cache, CDN and Script Manager settings) wait for your approval in WordPress before they run.
  • Every action an AI app takes is listed under AI → Activity. API keys and passwords are never shown to an AI app, and you can disconnect any app in one click.
  • Built on the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), on your own site, with no account or service of ours in between.

🌍 Languages

The plugin screen is translated into Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Dutch. Help translate it into your language on translate.wordpress.org.

🔒 Never cached, automatically

So carts, logins and private pages always stay correct:

  • Logged-in users (unless you turn on their private copies) and recent commenters.
  • Cart, checkout, account and receipt pages of WooCommerce, FluentCart and Easy Digital Downloads, and shoppers who have a cart.
  • Search results, previews, password-protected and private pages, page-builder editors.
  • Form submissions and any request that isn’t a normal page view; pages that set a cookie.
  • Any page where another plugin asks for no caching with the standard DONOTCACHEPAGE constant.

🤝 Contribute

Softminal Cache is developed and maintained by Softminal. Contributions are welcome: report a bug, suggest a feature or send a pull request on GitHub.

If another caching plugin is active, deactivate it first; two page caches fight each other.

Third-party services

Softminal Cache collects no data and has no service of its own. Only the features below make outside requests, and only after you turn them on:

  • Test cache, Preload, speed audit, self-check: these load pages of your own site (home_url()). Nothing goes anywhere else.
  • CDN (Cache → CDN, off by default): the Test button loads one WordPress core file (wp-includes/js/jquery/jquery.min.js) from the CDN address you entered. When the CDN is on, visitors load your files from that CDN, under its own terms and privacy policy. The plugin sends it nothing else.
  • Cloudflare (Cache → CDN, Cloudflare and Bunny, off until you connect): with your API token, the plugin calls api.cloudflare.com. It finds your site’s zone and clears Cloudflare’s cache when this plugin clears its own (changed page addresses, or everything). Nothing else is sent. Cloudflare terms and privacy policy.
  • Bunny (Cache → CDN, Cloudflare and Bunny, off until you connect): with your API key, the plugin calls api.bunny.net. It finds the pull zone for this site and clears it when this plugin clears everything. Nothing else is sent. If you use that pull zone as your CDN, visitors load your files from Bunny. bunny.net terms and privacy policy.
  • Keep Gravatar pictures on your site (Optimize → Images, off by default): your server downloads each Gravatar picture once from secure.gravatar.com, the address WordPress already uses. It then serves the picture from your site and refreshes it weekly. Nothing else is sent. Gravatar terms and privacy policy.
  • Google PageSpeed (Dashboard, only when you click Check with Google): the plugin sends one of your page addresses and your free Google API key to www.googleapis.com. Google tests that page and sends back the results, which stay on your site. Nothing runs in the background. PageSpeed Insights API terms and Google’s privacy policy.
  • Host Google Fonts on your site (Optimize → Fonts, off by default): your server downloads the fonts your theme already uses from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, once. Your site then serves them, so visitors stop connecting to Google. Google Fonts terms and privacy policy.

  • AI access (the AI tab, off by default): the plugin never calls an AI service itself. When you connect an AI app (for example Claude by Anthropic, ChatGPT by OpenAI, or Cursor or VS Code with the model you choose), that app sends requests to your site. The plugin answers only what the app is allowed to see:

    • cache status and settings (never API keys, tokens or passwords)
    • page check, speed audit and PageSpeed results
    • settings history and database counts
    • the last lines of the debug log, if it is on, with secrets removed

    This information goes to the company behind the app, under its own terms and privacy policy: Anthropic terms and privacy policy, OpenAI terms and privacy policy. Apps that connect by address sign in with standard OAuth 2.1. You approve them on a page of your own WordPress, and their key works only for this site and only for what you allowed. Disconnect any app under AI → Connected apps.
